summary: Specifies the Echo service, which sends back to the sender any data it receives. It is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it.

plainLanguage.summary: The Echo Protocol sends data back to the computer that sent it. It can use a continuing TCP connection or return one UDP message for each UDP message it receives.

questions: what port does the echo service use
what is the udp echo service
subtitle: A simple TCP or UDP service that sends received data back to its sender.

tldr.problem: A simple service is useful for debugging and measuring whether a network path can carry data.
tldr.mechanism: An Echo server listens on port 7 and returns the data it receives, using a TCP stream or an answering UDP datagram.
tldr.outcome: The RFC defines the behavior for hosts that choose to implement the Echo Protocol. The same data is returned without interpretation.

today: RFC 862 is listed as an Internet Standard in the unit metadata. The metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes it.

sections.title: A Basic Test Service
sections.content:
An echo service sends back any data it receives. The RFC describes it as a useful tool for debugging and measurement.

Hosts that choose to implement the protocol are expected to follow the behavior described in this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: The service returns the data sent to it. This makes it a simple way to check a network connection.

sections.title: Echo over TCP and UDP
sections.content:
For TCP, a server listens on TCP port 7. After a connection is established, it sends back any data received and continues until the user ends the connection.

For UDP, a server listens on UDP port 7. For each datagram it receives, it sends the same data back in an answering datagram.
sections.plainLanguage: With TCP, the server returns data over the open connection until the user ends it. With UDP, each message sent to the server gets a matching message back.

sections.title: The Echoed Data
sections.content: The service returns the received data to its source. The RFC does not describe additional processing or require a particular message format.
sections.plainLanguage: The server sends back the data it received, without changing the service into a more complex exchange.
